mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last 3 months signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a strong demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of overall economic growth, thus driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the housing starts are increasing.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and corporate costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where industrial production is declining.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure during a tightening monetary cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening cycle with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k MoM and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially during an early-cycle expansion.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where real GDP is increasing.
